mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has stabilized at -9.0% over the last two weeks after declining from -19.7%, signaling recovery of commuting patterns. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES declines below -15% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has converged toward baseline (-1.9% at t-0w from -3.1% at t-3w), indicating normalized essential shopping. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM stabilization, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below -4.0% in any of the next two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 9.3 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing -35%, or TRANSIT falls below -38% in the next week.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 20.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above the last-28-day mean despite PARKS remaining below -12%, or PARKS recovers above -5% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at 4.0-4.1% over the last two weeks after peaking at 7.4% (t-2w). This stabilization of at-home time, combined with modest workplace recovery (-9.0%), indicates a mixed-regime environment where consumers are neither fully confined nor fully mobile. Under this regime, retail-and-recreation mobility will remain suppressed relative to baseline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains between 3.5% and 5.5% AND WORKPLACES remains between -12% and -6%
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stabilized at 4.0-4.1% over last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above the last-28-day mean, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 2.0% or WORKPLACES improves above -5% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility has recovered 9.3 points over three weeks (-42.0% to -32.7%), while workplace mobility has improved 10.7 points (-19.7% to -9.0%). Under active reopening regimes, retail-and-recreation venues experience accelerated foot traffic within one week of sustained transit-and-workplace co-improvement.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by >5 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 10.7 points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of synchronized TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improvement, or either series declines by >3 points in the following week.

Seasonal suppression of outdoor activity correlates with suppressed retail-and-recreation mobility as consumers reduce discretionary outings. This seasonal drag will persist over the next four weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC below baseline.
